title: Independent complete source-image collation of Paris 1606 post-Canon tail and appended Suffragium
reviewer: Independent AI source-image reviewer (Paris 1606 post-Canon complete extent)
scope: Complete bounded printed post-Canon tail and appended Suffragium of the Paris 1606 Cistercian missal. It begins with Orémus/Præcéptis on printed p. 197 left, immediately after and excluding the accepted strict Canon’s final Per omnia/Amen. The main Ordinary tail closes on printed p. 199 right with the departure rubric Sicque signans se, & inclinans recedat. The appended Suffragium pro pace Ecclesiastica & temporali on printed p. 200 is included through its final Amen before INCIPIT SANCTORALE on p. 201. The appendix is printed after the main closure but its own rubric assigns recitation after the Canon’s Pater noster; units retain physical source order rather than silently relocating it. This is a bounded composite functional selection, not an assertion of an uninterrupted printed chapter or complete Ordinary. All in-scope prayers, abbreviated incipits, rubrics, response cues, crosses and sung words are included under the disclosed normalization. The prior 7-unit offertory and 35-unit Canon remain unchanged. Whole-Missal and complete-Ordinary text coverage remain partial; no wording or ancestry is inherited.
method: A reviewer distinct from both source authors directly inspected the original embedded JPEGs and native-pixel detail crops. The complete constituent was collated against every source word, actual accent, declared abbreviation expansion, punctuation/intonation mark, rubric, cross, response cue and meaningful paragraph on printed 197–200. No OCR, familiar formulary, or other edition controlled a reading. All 169 source text lines (55 on 197–198 and 114 on 199–200) and all 64 final units were reconciled. Final bodies equal the reviewed author readings with only the source-required pręséntibus correction; the p199 response receives its distinct semantic ID without wording change. Every final selected-line hash/range and page/unit census was checked. All five facsimile embedded JPEG hashes match the inspected source images; page 5 is outside-constituent boundary evidence.

findings_resolved.resolution: Source images were inspected and the extent/source-block census frozen before either author draft was opened. Start Orémus/Præceptis on printed 197; main closure Sicque...recedat on 199; appended Suffragium through final Amen on 200. Printed 201 Sanctorale and pre-start Canon words are excluded.
Corrected initial e-cauda in Libera from preséntibus to pręséntibus after direct native-pixel inspection. The second e retains its printed acute; no æ substitution is made.
Directly confirmed source déxterę in Hostium, distinct from the nearby explicit æ ligature of tuæ. U+0119 preserves the e-cauda.

All eight raised hook/zigzag-over-dot source signs on printed 200 are retained by the disclosed normalized U+2E4E ⹎ mapping. Their positions are after nos, Reges, tuæ, tua, meam, vobíscum, libertáte and nostrum. This mapping claims neither exact typeface identity nor historical/prosodic function.
All three printed crosses on 198 and both actual ℟. cues on 197 and 199 are retained; no response label is supplied on 198 or 200 where none is printed.

All 64 source-order prayer, rubric, response, incipit and paragraph blocks are retained, including inline dans dicat and Post sumptionem, Qui tecum as its own paragraph, and the separately bounded short incipits. The two different Pax responses remain distinct units.

Confirmed double-accent glóriósa, unaccented intercedente, eleíson, actual abbreviated endings, unpunctuated sung Amen on 197 and unpunctuated Deus on 198, repeated Agnus forms, ordinary question mark in Quid retribuam, and unusual quem tam sancta without harmonization.

The detached angled ink speck before Antequam is not a star/cue. INCIPIT on 200 is the catchword leading to Sanctorale 201. Both remain image context rather than literal prayer text. Running heads, foliation, signatures, geometry and chant notation are declared excluded while all selected sung words remain.

The p200 Suffragium remains after the p199 main closure in physical source order, while its complete printed rubric directs recitation after Pater noster Canonis. Neither position is silently substituted for the other.

normalization_limit: Direct original-image normalized reading transcription, not a glyph-diplomatic or musical edition. Long s becomes s; detached display initials join the word in sentence case; source wraps and line-end word divisions join within semantic blocks. Clear nasal suspensions, standard -us and -que brevigraphs expand without adding unprinted accents. Printed u/v, j, æ/œ, e-cauda ę, actual accents (including glóriósa, pręséntibus, déxterę and eleíson), punctuation, ampersands and abbreviated prayer endings remain. Distinct source prayer, rubric, response, incipit and paragraph blocks are separate source-order units; inline source boundaries are mapped in the census. The printed red crosses serialize as ✠ and the actual crossed-R cues as ℟. with their source period; no response cue is added where none is printed. Eight repeated raised hook/zigzag-over-dot signs in the p.200 appendix serialize as U+2E4E ⹎ (PUNCTUS ELEVATUS MARK), a disclosed normalized codepoint mapping from the observed source form, without claiming exact typeface identity, prosody or historical function. Repeated Agnus forms and short Psalmus/Lætatus sum/Gloria/Kyrie/Pater incipits remain as actually printed, without supplied continuations. All selected sung words remain; musical notes/staves, repeated running heads, foliation, signatures, catchwords including INCIPIT, ornament, ink colour, imposed line/column geometry and detached ink specks are excluded. The appendix remains in physical printing order after the p.199 main Order closure, although its rubric directs recitation after Pater noster Canonis. Every unit occupies one UTF-8 NFC physical payload line, ending with LF in the artifact; each unit text hash excludes that LF. No OCR, other-edition wording, familiar Roman wording or unprinted ending is supplied.
review_limit: Complete declared bounded post-Canon tail and printed appendix only. Main Order closure, physical appendix placement and instructed recitation position remain distinct. The strict Canon’s preceding final Amen and Sanctorale page 201 are excluded. Whole-Missal and complete-Ordinary coverage remain partial. This is a normalized reading transcription, not a glyph-diplomatic or musical edition; exact typeface geometry, pitches, historical ancestry and contemporary liturgical authorization are not asserted.
